text: Homeowners like Maria hate paying before a leak is fixed.
Plumbers like Luis hate waiting 45 days to get paid.
In home repair, trust is broken on both sides.
VeriPay fixes this.
PayPal holds the money, AI checks the work, and the pro is paid the moment every condition passes.
Maria tells her agent what's wrong, in one sentence.
Our model writes a definition of done:
what to fix, and the photo or note that proves it, priced against similar jobs.
Five pros' agents bid.
Maria's agent counters at $170, the pro comes back at $185, and her agent hires inside a signed mandate capped at $200.
A mandate capped lower, or sent twice, is refused.
PayPal authorizes and holds $200.
Nothing is charged.
The plumber knows the money is there before he drives out.
On site, the pro finds a corroded valve and asks for $47.05 more.
That's over her agent's limit, so only Maria can approve it, with her PIN.
PayPal re-holds $247.05.
The plumber sends his photos and the parts receipt from his phone.
Our models read the photos and the receipt.
Code checks when and where each photo was taken.
And when someone hides an instruction in a note, it's flagged, and the money waits for a person.
Every check passed, so code captures exactly $232.05, releases the rest, and one PayPal Payouts batch pays the pro.
Nobody pressed a button.
It scales past one faucet:
materials change orders, Pay Later, landlords and tenants, and neighbors booking together.
Operators see every hold, payout and dispute in AG Grid, reconciled against PayPal by an agent.
We attacked it for 11 rounds with 45 AI agents, as customers, pros and attackers.
Every blocker they found was fixed.
VeriPay.
The money waits for the proof.
